meta.description: Head of Research with three researchers

prompt.t:
Read and follow the common brief at C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\common.txt (read it first, fully). You are R1. CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r1. You own NEW files src/oscillations.rs and src/bin/r1_*.rs only.

TASK: Brain oscillations (alpha/beta/gamma/theta) in the mesh, as measurable opt-in wrappers around the existing Router (wrap warm-started robust Hebbian: see shortlab.rs for how it's built) and benchmarked in sim.rs Scenario variants and drift/failure windows. Hypotheses:
(a) ALPHA = periodic inhibition of exploration: oscillating temperature/epsilon schedule (e.g. period P tasks, duty cycle) vs constant temp; sweep P and amplitude on seeds 1-8.
(b) GAMMA synchrony: only agents whose recent-success phase is coherent (e.g. EMA of success above threshold, tracked on a gamma cycle) are recruited; weight consolidation (apply batched Hebbian update) every G tasks vs online.
(c) THETA-GAMMA coupling: working-memory slots, k items per theta cycle, replay recent outcomes (task,agent,reward) into the router at theta boundaries; test replay on/off, k in {2,4,8}.
(d) BETA status-quo: stickiness bonus to the currently routed agent per task type until a surprise burst (reward prediction error beyond threshold) releases it.
Plus a combined stack only if singles show promise. Each wrapper implements the Router trait. Include controls: a constant-phase (non-oscillating) variant with same average temp, and a phase-randomized oscillation, to show any gain is from the oscillation structure and not just a retuned temperature. Evaluate on all available Scenario variants plus failure/drift windows. Write results/r1_oscillations.json. Report honestly if nothing beats warm(hebbian-robust).

Read and follow the common brief at C:\Users\mariu\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\C--Users-mariu\8f3352b3-40ab-4151-abc9-d1de1978973c\scratchpad\common.txt (read it first, fully). You are R3. CARGO_TARGET_DIR=C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-r3. You own NEW files src/workmem.rs, src/spatial.rs, src/bin/r3_*.rs only (tiered.rs/lessons.rs belong to another in-progress agent; memory.rs read-only: use its public HNSW/flat index APIs).

TASK: Memory and spatial cognition.
(1) Working memory: bounded slot buffer (capacity K, e.g. 4/7/9) with chunking/compression of recurring task contexts; effect on routing in worlds with RECURRING task contexts (build a workload generator with recurring contexts in your bin, plus use sim.rs scenarios). Measure routing success vs fair baselines (see common brief), vs no-buffer, vs unbounded buffer; include a control with no recurrence.
(2) Persistent on-disk shared memory store ("shared memory folder"): append-only log + index (flat and/or HNSW from memory.rs, or memory-mapped if possible without new dependencies) with fast retrieval; measure latency (p50/p99), recall@k vs exact, bytes on disk, and warm-open time vs full reload/rebuild, crash-safety (truncated tail record is recovered), multi-reader sanity. Use std only; no new crates unless audited per the security rule.
(3) Spatial memory: 2D/3D coordinates; k-d tree and uniform grid index; queries: nearest-object, k-NN, range, path length (e.g. Manhattan/A* on a grid), layout overlap (AABB). Property tests against brute force with correctness tests; benchmark speedup vs brute force at several N. Optional "visual-spatial tasks" as task features for the router.
Report HONESTLY whether any of this improves ROUTING outcomes (held-out seeds 31-60, paired CI, Holm) or only speed/memory. Write results/r3_memory_spatial.json. Optional (security rule applies): hnswlib/faiss-cpu may be audited and used only to cross-check recall numbers, in the isolated venv; otherwise no packages.

user.t:
You are the HEAD OF RESEARCH for the neural-mesh project (Rust crate C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh). ALL decisions go through you: you assign work, approve or reject every result, and decide what is recommended for merge. Read first: DESIGN.md, results/experiment_output.txt (robustness study, Holm-corrected), results/shortlab.json (warm-start win), results/router_lab.json, results/memory.json, src/router.rs, src/sim.rs, src/stats.rs, src/memory.rs, src/prior.rs.

What the evidence says so far: the useful brain is a warm-started (keyword prior) robust Hebbian router (eta .01, temp .002, decay .01, eps 0) plus health benching; team/edge learning added nothing under fair evaluation; R-STDP, PG-actor, UCB, feature weighting, case-based embeddings did not beat fair baselines; HNSW gives 7.7x faster memory lookup at 97.6% recall. Another team (a hive queen with router/mesh/SONA workers) is concurrently editing src/hebbian.rs, src/prior.rs, src/mesh.rs, src/variants.rs, src/sona.rs and bin/w1_*/w2_*/w3_* — your team must NOT edit those, nor sim.rs, stats.rs, experiment.rs, shortlab.rs, main.rs, serve.rs, memory.rs, tiered.rs, lessons.rs, baselines.rs (read-only use via public APIs is fine).

Toolchain for every Bash call: export PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:/c/Users/mariu/AppData/Local/Microsoft/WinGet/Packages/BrechtSanders.WinLibs.POSIX.UCRT_Microsoft.Winget.Source_8wekyb3d8bbwe/mingw64/bin:$PATH" and a unique CARGO_TARGET_DIR per agent (C:/Users/mariu/nm-target-hr, -r1, -r2, -r3).

COMMUNICATION: keep a shared research board at C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\research_board.md — each researcher appends findings, numbers and questions; you append decisions (APPROVED / REJECTED / REDIRECT + reason). Use SendMessage to researchers for redirections.

SECURITY RULE (from the user, mandatory for everyone): before installing ANY package (PyPI, crates.io, npm), download it without executing anything (e.g. `pip download --no-deps --no-binary=:none:` / inspect the wheel or sdist; `carg
[...]
thm stays in Rust.

ACCEPTANCE BAR (you enforce it): a change is "better" only if, tuned on seeds 1-8 only, it beats the current best on held-out seeds 31-60 with paired 95% t-CI excluding 0 against the best fair baseline set {keyword, eps-greedy, pooled-thompson, hebbian-robust, warm(hebbian-robust)}, Holm-corrected across the family tested, in more than one world, and `cargo test --release --lib` stays green. Negative results are valuable — record them plainly. New behaviour must be opt-in (#[serde(default)], defaults unchanged). No git commits — the lead verifies and commits.

Spawn exactly 3 researchers (Task tool, nested depth 1; they must not spawn agents). Translate the user's wishes into measurable, testable mechanisms — no vague claims:
R1 — Brain oscillations (alpha/beta/gamma/theta) in the mesh. Own new files src/oscillations.rs, src/bin/r1_*.rs. Concrete hypotheses to test, e.g.: (a) alpha = periodic inhibition of exploration (oscillating epsilon/temperature schedule vs constant), (b) gamma synchrony = only agents whose recent-success "phase" is coherent get recruited / weights consolidate on a gamma cycle, (c) theta-gamma coupling = working-memory slots (k items per theta cycle) for which past tasks are replayed into the router (replay of recent outcomes), (d) beta = status-quo maintenance (stickiness bonus to the current routing until a surprise burst). Each as an opt-in wrapper around the existing router/mesh API; benchmark in the existing worlds (sim.rs Scenario variants) and drift/failure windows.
R2 — Cognitive skills: creativity, logic/science, design/UI-UX, business planning, marketing. Own new files src/cognition.rs, src/bin/r2_*.rs. Build a seeded multi-domain world inside your own binary: task domains {coding, science, design/ui-ux, business, marketing} × skills, multi-step tasks (plan→build→critique) where some domains reward DIVERSITY (creative tasks: value = quality × novelty vs recent solutions) and others reward CORRECTNESS (logic/science: verification step catches errors). Test mechanisms: quality-diversity routing (MAP-Elites style archive of agent×approach niches), novelty bonus for creative domains only, generator→critic sequencing for logic domains (critic agent chosen by learned reliability), domain-hierarchical routing (domain → specialist). Compare against the fair baselines on the same world.
R3 — Memory and spatial cognition. Own new files src/workmem.rs, src/spatial.rs, src/bin/r3_*.rs (tiered.rs/lessons.rs belong to another in-progress agent — read-only). Test: working-memory capacity (bounded slot buffer with chunking/compression) and its effect on routing with recurring task contexts; a persistent on-disk shared memory store ("shared memory folder") with fast retrieval (memory-mapped or append-only + HNSW/flat index) measured in latency, recall and bytes vs reloading; spatial memory (2D/3D coordinates: k-d tree or grid index for spatial queries; "visual-spatial" tasks such as nearest-object, path-length or layout-overlap queries) with correctness tests. Report honestly whether any of it improves routing outcomes, or only speed/memory.
Optionally (your decision) one PyPI comparison: if a highly-rated package is a credible reference for an idea (e.g. pyribs for MAP-Elites, river or mabwiser for bandits, hnswlib/faiss-cpu for ANN, brian2 for oscillations), audit it per the security rule and use it only to cross-check numbers.

Run the 3 researchers in parallel, review every claim yourself (rerun their benchmark binaries, check CIs, check the world isn't rigged in favour of the new mechanism — e.g. a novelty bonus that only helps in a world built to reward novelty must also be tested where it shouldn't help), give at most one follow-up round each, and finish within ~60 minutes. Final report to the lead: per researcher — hypotheses, held-out numbers, your APPROVED/REJECTED decision with reasons, files changed, packages audited (and any security findings), and a ranked list of what to merge.

handback.t:
HEAD OF RESEARCH FINAL REPORT (neural-mesh). Board with all decisions: C:\Users\mariu\neural-mesh\results\research_board.md. I reran every claim myself in separate target dirs (nm-target-hr, -hr2, -hr3). `cargo test --release --lib` = 168 passed, 0 failed (my run, end of session). Acceptance bar: tune seeds 1-8, held-out 31-60, paired 95% CI vs best fair baseline, Holm, >1 world, tests green, opt-in.

== RESEARCHERS ==
R1 oscillations (src/oscillations.rs, src/bin/r1_oscillations.rs, results/r1_oscillations.json): REJECTED. Alpha, gamma (gate/batch), theta-gamma replay and beta were tested. 0 Holm wins over warm(hebbian-robust) across 4 sim scenarios + a static control (154 cells). Controls (mean-matched constant, phase-random, random-time) match or beat the oscillating versions, so there is no oscillation-structure effect. Beta significantly hurts (-0.019 fixed, -0.013 no-traps, -0.013 static). HEAD rerun was byte-identical. Keep only as an opt-in negative-result module (off == plain Warm).

R2 cognition (src/cognition.rs, src/bin/r2_cognition.rs, results/r2_cognition.json): REJECTED as a routing improvement. The system (hierarchy + QD niche archive + fair critic) beats the best fair baseline only in worlds A (+0.032) and C (+0.028). Those two share the same specialist/multimodal structure, so they count as 1 independent world, and A favours creative mechanisms by construction. It loses in B (-0.012) and D (-0.019). The learned critic does not beat the warm bandit as critic selector. Useful design finding: a creative-only novelty bonus is harmless elsewhere, whereas applying novelty to all domains costs -0.04 on correctness. The rigged-check world D works as intended. Rerun byte-identical. pyribs cross-check was not done, so there is no package audit.

R3 memory/spatial (src/workmem.rs, src/spatial.rs, src/bin/r3_{workmem,store,spatial}.rs, results/r3_memory_spatial.json):
 - Working-memory router: CONDITIONALLY APPROVED, opt-in only. Holm wins over warm in 4/4 recurring-context worlds (+0.06 to +0.09; chunking +0.078), reproduced by HEAD. The worlds are the author's own, with explicit context labels. The gain comes from having context-keyed memory, not from boundedness. It HURTS when contexts don't recur or don't matter (-0.013 to -0.13), and sim:fixed K=2 looks like a window-label leak. It needs a fall-back guard before any use; not for defaults.
 - Persistent store (append-only log + snapshot, flat/HNSW, CRC, crash recovery 150/150, 1 writer + 4 readers clean): APPROVED as infrastructure (speed and robustness only, no routing effect). Flat is the better default at N=30k, since HNSW is only 1.3-2.5x faster at ~11x memory.
 - spatial.rs (k-d tree, grid, A*, AABB; property-tested vs brute force; up to ~2800x k-NN at N=1e5): APPROVED as infrastructure.
 - Spatial features as router inputs: REJECTED (hebbian-robust -0.022 Holm; -0.05 to -0.10 in the control).

== VERIFY REQUESTS (Hebbian router / mesh changes) ==
 - router-thinker guarded(hebr) (prior.rs `Guarded`, opt-in; hebbian.rs opt-in Median/Kalman, default Sum unchanged): VERIFIED. HEAD reran x1_lab on 31-60 and on 61-90 (fresh seeds), results identical apart from a timing field. traps H100 +0.020 [+.0105,+.0295] (Holm p=.012) and +0.017 on 61-90; many-topics16 H250-H2000 +0.013 to +0.034 vs best fair baseline (Holm WIN); 0 Holm losses. Small non-significant cost vs keyword (-0.001 to -0.006) where keywords are correct. Caveats: the gain is mainly in early/sparse-data horizons (hand-over to the keyword prior). The author disclosed one quick-grid held-out peek followed by an objective change; the 61-90 confirmation mitigates that. kalman(kw) and guarded(kalman) are NOT recommended (losses or less robust per the author's own data).
 - mesh-thinker SecondOpinion gate (variants.rs, opt-in): VERIFIED CONDITIONALLY. Rerun identical. Net-of-cost gain +0.012/+0.011 at c=.05 in v-fixed/v-random (Holm p<1e-4), and the gate beats always-check and rate-matched random checking. The world is the author's own verification world. The gate is WORSE in v-notraps (-0.011 vs keyword at c=.10), with weak checkers (-0.001) and with no useful checkers (-0.002). Router picks are unchanged. Use only where real verifiers exist; not a default.
 - mesh-thinker ContextBench (mesh.rs H3): REJECTED. No win vs best baseline in any of 5 worlds; the author did not submit it.
 - lessons-from-mistakes (lessons.rs/tiered.rs, via lead): NOT VERIFIED, rejected for merge. memory_lab rerun reproduces the numbers, but the comparator router (eta .05, T .02, success ~.62-.69) is far below warm(hebbian-robust) (~.77). The gain looks like generic success tracking (attribution not significant). It needs a comparison against warm and against a more exploratory router before it can pass.
 - x3 coupling (coupling.rs): no VERIFY REQUEST was posted, so it is NOT verified. results/x3_coupling*.json exist. Earlier 3 coupling:: test failures reported by R2 are gone; the lib suite is green.

== RANKED MERGE LIST ==
 1. x1 guarded(hebr) (prior.rs Guarded + opt-in hebbian.rs Median/Kalman, x1_lab) - the only verified improvement to the router. Merge opt-in.
 2. workmem::store and spatial.rs - infrastructure, correct and tested; merge, no routing claims. Prefer flat index at this scale.
 3. x2 SecondOpinion - opt-in, conditional on verifiers; merge only with that documentation.
 4. workmem router - opt-in experiment only, needs a fall-back guard.
 5. Do NOT merge as functional features: oscillations (keep as negative-result code), cognition (research module), spatial router features, ContextBench, lessons (until compared to warm), x3 until verified.

== PACKAGES / SECURITY ==
No researcher installed any package or added any dependency; no Python venv was used, and the optional pyribs/hnswlib/faiss cross-checks were not done. No security findings. One observation for the lead: Cargo.toml (last modified 02:47, before this session's work) lists many third-party neural/SNN crates (axicor-*, ruv-neural-*, neuralos-snn, synaptic-neural-*, thermogram, turbovec, etc.). Only `neural_mesh` and `oxicuda_snn` appear in src `use` lines, so most appear unused. They were not audited by my team; I recommend pruning or auditing them per the user's security rule.

Files created by my team (all new, plus appended `pub mod` lines in src/lib.rs): src/oscillations.rs, src/cognition.rs, src/workmem.rs, src/spatial.rs, src/bin/r1_oscillations.rs, r2_cognition.rs, r3_workmem.rs, r3_store.rs, r3_spatial.rs; results r1_oscillations.json, r2_cognition.json, r3_memory_spatial.json, r3_*_output.txt, research_board.md. No git commits were made.
